themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK versus a 2.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 736% increase (z-score 8.31)—signaling a sudden, coordinated vandalism surge or enforcement gap in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints this week vs. 2.8 weekly average (736% spike, z-score 8.31)
Represents the sharpest statistical deviation among all 311 categories monitored
Spike is CURRENT (this week), not historical
reporting_angles: Is this a coordinated tagging campaign by a specific crew, or has NYPD/Sanitation enforcement lapsed in certain blocks?
Interview residents on heavily tagged blocks; photograph hot spots and interview local business owners about impact and costs

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Removal Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a 1.6 weekly baseline—a 269% surge (z-score 5.11)—suggesting possible sanitation workforce shortage, disease vector concern, or seasonal die-off requiring immediate pickup.
evidence: 6 dead animal complaints this week vs. 1.6 weekly average (269% spike, z-score 5.11)
Public health and neighborhood quality-of-life concern emerging in real time
Spike is CURRENT (this week), most recent data point after graffiti
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation about response times and staffing; investigate if there's a disease or predator issue (rats, wildlife) driving animal deaths
Walk affected blocks; photograph conditions; interview residents about health concerns and how long carcasses remain

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Obstructions Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints rose to 3 THIS WEEK from a 1.1 weekly average—a 167% spike (z-score 5.67)—indicating potential illegal vendor encroachment, construction debris, or sidewalk blockage affecting pedestrian access.
evidence: 3 obstruction complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average (167% spike, z-score 5.67)
Emerging THIS WEEK, same timeframe as graffiti and dead animal spikes
Pattern suggests street-level disorder may be multi-faceted rather than isolated
reporting_angles: Map obstruction complaints geographically; identify if they cluster around specific intersections, parks, or transit hubs
Interview 311 data analysts and NYPD enforcement teams about whether these are construction-related, vendor-related, or homeless encampment-related

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.9 weekly average—a 243% spike (z-score 6.43)—suggesting surge in unlicensed ride-share activity, unsafe driving, or illegal parking by Uber/Lyft vehicles in the district.
evidence: 3 for-hire vehicle complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (243% spike, z-score 6.43)
Emerging THIS WEEK alongside other street-level disorder signals
Complements long-running illegal parking problem (2,018 complaints over 90 days, high baseline)
reporting_angles: Are complaints about unsafe driving, congestion, or illegal street parking by ride-share vehicles? Interview TLC enforcement about coverage in Flatbush/PLG
Monitor whether this connects to broader taxi/TLC enforcement activity or reflects genuine uptick in unregulated vehicles

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly average—a 1100% spike (z-score 6.35)—indicating either a loose pack, new dog owners post-pandemic, or enforcement gap in parks and residential areas.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Spike is recent (last week) but slightly older than this week's graffiti, dead animal, and obstruction signals
Highest statistical magnitude but slightly less current than above three issues
reporting_angles: Identify specific parks or neighborhoods where unleashed dogs were reported; interview Parks Enforcement and NYPD about response
Human-interest angle: interview residents (especially families with kids) about safety concerns; identify whether this is a specific dog owner problem or systemic enforcement lapse
